He played [[college basketball]] for the [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU Tigers]]. He played in the NBA for the [[Chicago Bulls]]. == Early life and high school career== Blakeney was born in [[Watertown, New York]], to Tequisha Blakeney. He has two brothers, Tyrieke Blakeney and Dontrez Jones.[https://lsusports.net/sports/mb/roster/player/antonio-blakeney/ "Antonio Blakeney,"] LSU Sports.{{cite web|url=https://usf.rivals.com/news/class-of-2015-prospect-antonio-blakeney|date=17 January 2013|work=rivals.com|accessdate=21 June 2019|title=Class of 2015 prospect – Antonio Blakeney|archive-date=21 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190621041530/https://usf.rivals.com/news/class-of-2015-prospect-antonio-blakeney|url-status=live}} Blakeney attended and played basketball for [[Oak Ridge High School (Orlando, Florida)|Oak Ridge]] in [[Orlando, Florida]]. In his senior year (2014-15) he averaged 29 points, 6.9 rebounds, and 2.7 assists per game. He was a [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2015 McDonald's All-American]], 2015 ''Slam Magazine'' All-American, [[Florida Mr. Basketball|Florida's Mr. Basketball]], Class 8A Player of the Year, and ''Orlando Sentinel'' 2015 all-area Player of the Year.{{Cite news|url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/blog/os-ben-simmons-antonio-blakeney-lead-east-to-victory-at-mcdonalds-allamerican-boys-basketball-game-20150401-story.html|title=Simmons, Blakeney lead East to victory at McDonald's All-American game|last=Kaberon|first=Eli|work=OrlandoSentinel.com|access-date=2017-05-26|language=en-US|archive-date=2019-01-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190124203833/https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/blog/os-ben-simmons-antonio-blakeney-lead-east-to-victory-at-mcdonalds-allamerican-boys-basketball-game-20150401-story.html|url-status=live}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.nola.com/lsu/index.ssf/2015/03/antonio_blakeney_ben_simmons.html|title=LSU-bound Antonio Blakeney named Florida Mr. Basketball ahead of Ben Simmons|work=NOLA.com|access-date=2017-05-26|language=en-US|archive-date=2019-01-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190125020356/https://www.nola.com/lsu/index.ssf/2015/03/antonio_blakeney_ben_simmons.html|url-status=live}} Blakeney was rated as a 5-star recruit by Rivals, ESPN, and 247 Sports. Rivals had him as the #13 overall recruit, while ESPN had him at #15, and 247 at #16. Both ESPN and 247 ranked him as the #3 SG in the nation.{{cite web|title=Antonio Blakeney Basketball Recruit|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2015/antonio-blakeney-7059|website=Rivals.com|accessdate=22 November 2017}}{{cite web|title=Basketball Recruiting – Antonio Blakeney|url=https://insider.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/166291/antonio-blakeney|website=ESPN|access-date=22 November 2017|archive-date=1 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201041544/http://insider.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/166291/antonio-blakeney|url-status=live}}{{cite web|title=Antonio Blakeney, Oak Ridge, Shooting Guard|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Antonio-Blakeney-22940/high-school-58895|website=247 Sports|accessdate=22 November 2017}} ==College career== Blakeney initially gave a verbal commitment to the [[University of Louisville]], but then he changed his mind about 10 days later and decommitted. Blakeney ended up committing to [[LSU Tigers basketball|Louisiana State University]], (LSU), where he majored in sports administration. At LSU he was featured in 34 games as a freshman, playing alongside [[Ben Simmons]]. Behind Simmons and [[Keith Hornsby]], Blakeney was LSU's third-leading scorer in 2015–16, averaging 12.6 points a contest,{{Cite web|url=https://www.todaysu.com/sec/lsu-tigers/antonio-blakeney-has-the-potential-to-be-a-star-for-lsu/|title=Antonio Blakeney Has The Potential To Be A Star For LSU – TU|website=www.todaysu.com|language=en-US|access-date=2017-05-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201035539/https://www.todaysu.com/sec/lsu-tigers/antonio-blakeney-has-the-potential-to-be-a-star-for-lsu/|archive-date=2017-12-01|url-status=dead}} hitting a team-best 52 three-point shots on the season. The 2016–17 season saw him emerge as LSU's leading scorer, pouring in 17.2 points per contest, while corralling 4.8 rebounds a game and handing out 1.7 assists per outing. Blakeney took home an All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] Second Team selection that year.{{Cite news|url=http://www.nola.com/lsu/index.ssf/2017/03/lsus_antonio_blakeney_named_se.html|title=LSU's Antonio Blakeney named second-team All-SEC|work=NOLA.com|access-date=2017-05-26|language=en-US|archive-date=2017-03-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170307205937/http://www.nola.com/lsu/index.ssf/2017/03/lsus_antonio_blakeney_named_se.html|url-status=live}} In April 2017, he announced that he would forego the remaining two years of his college eligibility and declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/19138140/lsu-top-scorer-antonio-blakeney-entering-nba-draft|title=Blakeney, LSU's top scorer, entering NBA draft|work=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-05-26|archive-date=2017-04-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170421103405/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/19138140/lsu-top-scorer-antonio-blakeney-entering-nba-draft|url-status=live}} ==Professional career== ===Chicago Bulls (2017–2019)=== After going undrafted, Blakeney joined the [[Chicago Bulls]] for the [[2017 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.csnmidatlantic.com/washington-wizards/2017-18-nba-undrafted-free-agent-list-summer-league-rosters|title=2017–18 NBA Undrafted Free Agent List: Summer League rosters|date=2017-06-23|work=CSN Mid-Atlantic|access-date=2017-07-01|archive-date=2017-07-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170701062533/http://www.csnmidatlantic.com/washington-wizards/2017-18-nba-undrafted-free-agent-list-summer-league-rosters?|url-status=live}} Based on his performance there, Blakeney was signed to a [[two-way contract]] by the Bulls. Under the terms of the deal, he split time between the Bulls and their [[NBA G League|G League]] affiliate, the [[Windy City Bulls]].{{cite news|title=BULLS SIGN BLAKENEY TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-blakeney-two-way-contract|accessdate=July 14, 2017|work=[[Chicago Bulls]]|date=July 14, 2017|archive-date=July 14, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170714190626/http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-blakeney-two-way-contract|url-status=live}} He made his professional debut with Chicago on October 19 against the [[Toronto Raptors]]. On November 21, 2017, Blakeney scored 15 points in 18 minutes off the bench in a 113–105 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{Cite played in China with the [[Jiangsu Dragons]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). He averaged 34.8 points (4th in the league), 8.0 rebounds, and 3.4 assists per game, while shooting 50.0% from the field. ===Canton Charge (2021)=== For the 2020–21 season, Blakeney signed with the [[Canton Charge]] of the G League.{{cite web |title=Charge Announce 2021 Roster |url=https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/charge-announce-2021-roster/ |website=NBA.com |accessdate=January 25, 2021 |date=January 22, 2021 |archive-date=January 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210124203010/https://canton.gleague.nba.com/news/charge-announce-2021-roster/ |url-status=live }} He averaged 15.1 points and 4.3 rebounds per game. In early 2021, Blakeney was arrested for armed robbery and bonded out of jail.{{Cite web |last=Writer |first=JULIA GUILBEAU {{!}} Staff |title=Former LSU basketball player Antonio Blakeney arrested on armed robbery in Florida: report |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/news/crime_police/article_32fd8298-bcb5-11eb-8ba6-9bc30391a6e7.html |access-date=2022-02-28 |website=The Advocate |date=May 24, 2021 |language=en}} ===Al Ahli Club of Manama (2022)=== On Jan, 2022, Blakeney signed with the [[Al-Ahli Club (Manama)|Al-Ahli]] of the [[Bahraini Premier League]]. On Jan 28, 2022, he scored a game-high 33 points in the 1st round against [[Al-Najma SC (Bahrain)|Al-Najma]]. ===Hapoel Be'er Sheva (2022)=== On March 17, 2022, he signed with [[Hapoel Be'er Sheva B.C.|Hapoel Be'er Sheva]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Israel/news/735635/Antonio-Blakeney-signed-with-Hapoel-Beer-Sheva|title=Antonio Blakeney signed with Hapoel Beer Sheva|last=|first=|date=March 17, 2022|website=|publisher=Eurobasket|language=En|access-date=March 2, 2022}} He played four games for the team, in which he averaged 24.5 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 4.0 assists per game, while shooting 49.3% from the field. === Jiangsu Dragons (2022–2023) === In the 2022–23 season, Blakeney played in China with the [[Jiangsu Dragons]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). He was the [[Chinese Basketball Association scoring leaders|scoring leader]] of the league after averaging 32.1 points per game, and had 7.4 rebounds and 4.8 assists per game, as he shot 82.8% from the free throw line.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/cba-china/2023.html. CBA 2022-23 Season] === Nanjing Monkey Kings (2023–2024) === Blakeney joined the [[Nanjing Monkey Kings]] for the 2023–24 CBA season. On December 29, 2023, he scored 50 points in a 124–99 win over [[Shanxi Loongs]], his fourth 50-point CBA game.{{Cite web |title=Blakeney's 50 gifts Nanjing easy win over Shanxi in CBA-Xinhua |url=https://english.news.cn/20231229/96598a789887433cbf137da100a8f30d/c.html |access-date=2024-04-01 |website=english.news.cn |archive-date=2024-04-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240401105743/https://english.news.cn/20231229/96598a789887433cbf137da100a8f30d/c.html |url-status=live }} He averaged 30.5 points (2nd in the league), 7.1 rebounds, and 4.3 assists per game, while shooting 49.7% from the field, 41.2% from three-point range, and 85.4% from the free throw line.[https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Antonio-Blakeney/Summary/72599 "Antonio Blakeney,"] RealGM. === Hapoel Tel Aviv (2024–present) === On October 21, 2024, Blakeney signed with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]] and [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].{{cite web |title=ברוך הבא, אנטוניו בלייקני! |url=https://www.hapoeluta.org/news?NewsId=36801 |website=מועדון הכדורסל הפועל "שלמה" תל אביב |access-date=21 October 2024 |date=21 October 2024}} On July 10, 2026, the team extended his contract until the summer of 2029.{{cite web |title=Blakeney “locked” with Hapoel Tel Aviv until the summer of 2029 |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1989968/blakeney-locked-with-hapoel-until-the-summer-of-2029/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=28 July 2026 |language=en |date=10 July 2026}} ==Personal life== In May 2021, Blakeney was arrested in Florida and charged with multiple offenses including home invasion robbery with a firearm, aggravated assault and grand theft. He was accused to arranging for a group of men to come to his house and rob another group of men who he had invited to play cards.{{cite news |last1=Machlin |first1=Tsvi |title=Former LSU Basketball
